subject: Monetary remedy structure request and next steps
body:
From: Anna Liu <anna.liu@helioshealth.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Jan 2027 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: SLA remedies — request for buyout / cash remedies beyond credits

Hi Camila,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Helios is moving fast on a pilot and procurement has surfaced two items they can’t accept as credits-only: 1) termination rights tied to repeated P1/P2 latency breaches and 2) a cash-based makeup/remedy if those breaches continue after cure.

Specifically, procurement asked whether we can include a buyout right if uptime/latency breaches persist over a defined window, and whether there can be a fixed-sum remedy (liquidated damages or fee-at-risk) beyond the standard monthly service credits the SLA provides. They want something that can be invoked without litigation complexity — a capped, contractually defined payment.

I’ve attached a short note with their suggested language and an ask for three months of average monthly fees as an upper bound. I know this is a bigger ask than standard, but wanted to surface it now before legal review.

Could you confirm Redwood’s tolerance for a fixed cash remedy or a staged buyout? If possible, include any precedent or a counter-structure that would be acceptable (e.g., escrowed holdback, staged cure + buyout, or fixed cap).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is on a tight cadence.

Best,
Anna Liu
SVP, Partnerships
Helios Health
attachments: Helios_SLA_monetary_ask_20270110.docx

On Mon, Jan 11, 2027 at 09:10 AM Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 11 Jan 2027 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for buyout / cash remedies beyond credits

Hi Anna — thanks for the note and the attachment. I pulled Marcus and Lauren into the thread so we can provide a coordinated response.

Short answer: we try to avoid cash-based liquidated damages tied solely to uptime/latency breaches, because that introduces an open-ended financial exposure and operational complexity. That said, we recognize Helios’s procurement needs and are open to a compromise that preserves operational predictability for both parties.

Possible options we can propose to legal:
- Staged cure + buyout: a defined cure period (30–60 days) after recurring P1 or P2 windows; if breaches persist, customer can buy out remaining term with a predefined formula (e.g., 2–3x monthly fees or remaining committed fees up to a cap).
- Escrowed holdback: small percentage of committed fees (e.g., 5–10%) held in escrow and released unless a defined threshold breach occurs.
- Fixed-cap cash remedy: allow a capped fixed-sum payment (e.g., equal to X months of fees) with clear triggers, explicit exclusions (force majeure, scheduled maintenance), and a cap on aggregate exposure.
- Enhanced service credits + remediation path: higher credits for repeat events, combined with technical remediation commitments and executive SLA reviews — keeps it credit-first but more meaningful.

We can prepare redline language for one of the above. If Helios’s procurement team is set on a cash remedy, we’d prefer a firm cap that’s a single-digit multiple of monthly fees and a requirement that Helios pursue the buyout only after a sequence of continued, documented breaches.

I’ll follow up with draft counter-language (Marcus, Lauren: can you advise on typical caps and wording?)

Best,
Camila
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

On Tue, Jan 12, 2027 at 14:52 Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Anna Liu <anna.liu@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 14:52:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for buyout / cash remedies beyond credits

Anna / Camila — I reviewed Helios’s proposed language. High-level guidance: we need a structure that caps our exposure, preserves standard exceptions, and limits the circumstances where a buyout or cash remedy is available. Below are redline-level suggestions I will push in the next draft: 

1) Triggering sequence: require at least three P1 or P2 incidents in a rolling 90-day window, each confirmed by incident post-mortem and shown not to be covered by scheduled maintenance or customer misconfiguration.
2) Cure timeline: 30 days from notice to cure systemic root causes; if unresolved after two successive cure periods, allow buyer to elect either (a) an accelerated termination (buyout) at a capped amount or (b) a one-time fixed cash remedy equal to 3 months average invoiced fees, not exceeding $300,000.
3) Aggregation cap: cap aggregate cash exposure to a single-sum equal to 6 months average fees or $500,000, whichever is lower.
4) Exclusions & mitigation: carve-outs for force majeure, major cloud provider outages, and customer-induced load; mandatory technical remediation plan and executive review before buyout election.
5) Audit rights: customer may request logs and evidence for incidents, but access limited to agreed scope and confidentiality protections.

If Helios wants a simpler approach, we can offer a single fixed-cap payment (e.g., 3 months fees) with the above triggers and a strict global cap. I’ll draft counter-redlines with exact phrasing and provide a PDF for review.

Marcus
Deputy General Counsel
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_counter_redlines_20270112.pdf

On Wed, Jan 13, 2027 at 11:08 AM Anna Liu <anna.liu@helioshealth.com> wrote:

Cc: Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 13 Jan 2027 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for buyout / cash remedies beyond credits

Camila/Marcus — thanks for the thoughtful options. Procurement reviewed Marcus’s proposal and asked for clarification on two points before they take it to the executive buyer: 1) If Helios elects the buyout option, what is the formula for remaining-term buyout (straight remaining committed fees vs. multiplier)? 2) Can the cap be expressed as a multiple of monthly fees rather than a hard $ number (procurement likes percentage-of-MRR math for benchmarking across vendors)?

Procurement also asked that the cure period be clearly documented in the contract and that the buyout option be available only once per 12-month period to avoid repeat buyouts.

If you can convert Marcus’s draft into clean contract text and share a short summary of the math (examples with $ figures), that would help accelerate internal approvals.

Thanks,
Anna

On Thu, Jan 14, 2027 at 17:05 Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com> wrote:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Anna Liu <anna.liu@helioshealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 17:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SLA remedies — request for buyout / cash remedies beyond credits

Anna — appreciate the clear feedback. We converted Marcus’s high-level structure into two contract-ready options and attached the redlines / worked examples for Helios to evaluate: 1) Staged-buyout formula (remaining committed fees with a 1.5x multiplier, capped at 4 months of average invoiced fees) and 2) Fixed-cap cash remedy (one-time payment equal to 3 months average fees; customer can elect in lieu of buyout). Both options include: a 30-day cure, a maximum of one buyout election per 12 months, exclusions for force majeure/cloud outage/customer misuse, and an aggregate exposure cap.

Summary math examples (worked cases included in PDF):
- Example A (annual commitment $600k, monthly $50k): staged buyout = remaining term * 1.5, capped at 4 * $50k = $200k.
- Example B (same commitment): fixed-cap remedy = 3 * $50k = $150k.

Next steps: Marcus will bake the exact clause language into the master services agreement redline. If procurement approves one of these two options, we’ll pass it to our contracting team and prepare a DocuSign package.

Anna / procurement: can you indicate preference (staged-buyout vs. fixed-cap) and confirm acceptance of the one-per-12-month limitation? If you prefer, we can also accept a percentage-of-MRR expression instead of hard numbers in the clause; just tell us the preferred multiple.

Thanks,
Camila
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
attachments: Redwood_counter_redlines_20270112.pdf
